correctness.rationale: For nonempty selected edges S the initially white vertices are exactly E(G[U]), U consisting of vertices not incident with S. For any observed boundary edge xy with y in U its white-neighbor count equals deg_{G[U]}(y). A complete multipartite residual H with an edge has a degree-one vertex exactly when precisely two parts remain nonempty and one has size one, hence H is a star; all its edges force in one parallel round because S touches two original parts. Otherwise either H is edgeless (zero rounds) or every nonisolated vertex has degree at least two (no legal force). Exact support-based inclusion-exclusion counts nonempty selected edge covers of each complement, with an explicit empty-support adjustment. Exhaustive independently computed forcing-round simulation agreed on 203826 subsets in 57 small positive-part tuples; 168672 subsets in 38 tuples belong to the newly claimed domain. Coefficients checked with independent inclusion-exclusion on eight instances. These finite checks supplement a complete argument, not infinite certification.

value.rationale: A complete classification for the natural new graph family of all mixed complete multipartite line graphs with three or more parts is neither a fixed numerical slice nor an already known boundary case. It exposes a genuine three-part obstruction to propagation, proves the zero-or-one forcing-round phenomenon in all parameters, and supplies a self-contained bivariate enumerator of successful placements by both cardinality and propagation behavior. The elementary edge-support method is acknowledged, but the mixed-part all-parameter enumeration and propagation-time refinement are not obtainable merely by substituting values into either earlier boundary-family theorem; the full distribution has plausible use in PMU placement and enumerative studies.
